--- order: 1 unit: page introduces: [script, js-query, text-content, style-prop, console-log] assumes: [heading, paragraph] title: Find and change summary: "Find an element on a page with JavaScript, change its text and colour, and read what the console says." language: html voice: { name: af_heart, speed: 1.1 } app: command: node "$REPO_ROOT/tools/serve.mjs" "$REPO_ROOT/dist/_playground-dom" 8131 url: http://127.0.0.1:8131/index.html ready: HTML and JavaScript code layout: full pacing: keyDelayMs: 30 explainPicture: page.html#run explainClip: query: {code: "", zoom: 1.4} caption: "JavaScript finds an element by its id, then changes it" clip: - caption: "A heading with an id, so JavaScript can find it." - type: {into: "HTML and JavaScript code", text: "

Sports day

\n", append: true} - caption: "A script runs when the browser reaches it, so it goes below the heading." - type: {into: "HTML and JavaScript code", text: "\n", append: true} - click: "Run ▶" - expect: {selector: "#status", contains: "Running"} - wait: 1100 - caption: text: "textContent changed the words and style.color the colour, while the page was open." say: "text Content changed the words, and style dot color changed the colour." hook: "The page is already on screen, and your code can still change any part of it." --- A web page is a tree of **elements**. JavaScript can find one and change it while the page is open. Two steps do most of the work: 1. **Find it**: `document.querySelector("#title")` finds the element with `id="title"`. A `#` means an id, a `.` means a class (`".note"`), and a plain word means a tag (`"h1"`). 2. **Change it**: `title.textContent = "New words"` replaces its text, and `title.style.color = "crimson"` changes its colour. `console.log(...)` writes a message in the **Console** under the page, to see what your code is doing. **The hard part** is the selector. It is just text, so a typo finds nothing: the answer is `null`, and the next line fails with "Cannot set properties of null". When you see `null`, check the selector first. ## Predict ```step stage: predict code: page.html#predict check: type: predict q: "What does the heading say once the page has loaded?" options: ["Sports day: moved to Friday", "Sports day", "Moved to Friday", "Nothing: a script cannot change a heading"] actual: "Sports day: moved to Friday. The script finds the heading and replaces its text, and console.log then writes the new text in the Console." ``` Does the script run before or after the heading has appeared? ## Run ```step stage: run code: page.html#run try: { playground: dom, starter: "page.html#run", height: 430 } check: { type: reflect, text: "I can see that JavaScript changed the heading and the note after the page loaded." } ``` Press **Run**. The page starts as plain HTML, and then the script changes two elements. The Console shows what `console.log` wrote. ## Investigate ```step stage: investigate code: page.html#run insight: "querySelector turns a selector into an element, and changing the element's properties changes the page; a selector that matches nothing gives null." tasks: - check: type: match q: "Match each line with what it does." pairs: - ["document.querySelector(\"#title\")", "finds the element with id title"] - ["document.querySelector(\".note\")", "finds the first element with class note"] - ["title.textContent = \"Moved\";", "replaces the words inside the element"] - ["console.log(title.textContent);", "writes the text in the Console, not on the page"] - check: type: question q: "Why is the script below the heading and not above it?" options: ["A script runs as soon as the browser reaches it, so the heading must already exist", "Scripts only work at the bottom of a file", "The heading would disappear otherwise", "It makes the page load faster"] answer: 0 explain: "The browser reads the page from the top. A script above the heading would run before the heading exists, so querySelector would find null." - check: type: bug code: page.html#bug text: "This stops with an error: Cannot set properties of null. Click the line that is the real cause." answer: 4 fault: runtime misconception: selector-typo explain: "The error shows on line 5, but the cause is line 4: the heading's id is title, so #titel finds nothing and title is null." ``` ### Which line does what? Match code with meaning. ### Script order The browser reads from the top. ### Spot the bug The error shows on one line and starts on another. ## Modify ```step stage: modify insight: "Every element has its own text and style; find it with its own selector." try: { playground: dom, starter: "page.html#run", height: 430 } tasks: - hint: - "The note has class note, so its selector starts with a dot." - "const note = document.querySelector(\".note\"); then note.textContent = \"…\";" expected: page.html#sol-note check: { type: code, text: "Change the note's words to bring sunscreen too.", rules: { contains: [".note", "textContent"] } } - hint: - "Style properties are on the element's style: title.style.color." - "The value is text, in quotes: title.style.color = \"crimson\";" expected: page.html#sol-colour check: { type: code, text: "Make the heading crimson.", rules: { contains: [".style.color"] } } ``` ### The note Change the note to say you should bring **sunscreen** too. ### Crimson Make the heading **crimson**. ## Make: change three things ```step stage: make insight: "Goals only: find three elements and change something about each." try: { playground: dom, starter: "page.html#make", height: 430 } check: { type: reflect, text: "My page changes three elements with JavaScript: some text, a colour and a size." } ``` Find **three elements** and change something about each: text, colour (`style.color`), size (`style.fontSize = "24px"`). Add more elements of your own to the page if you like. ## Where this leads ```step stage: info check: type: question q: "You want the heading to change only when someone clicks a button. What is missing?" options: ["Code that waits for the click and then runs the change", "A longer script", "A second heading", "Nothing: scripts already wait for clicks"] answer: 0 explain: "A script runs once, as the page loads. To wait for a click you give the button a function to run when the click happens: an event listener. Next lesson." ``` Your code can now find and change anything on a page. Next: make it happen **when someone clicks**. ```teacher summary: Students find an element with querySelector, change its text and colour from JavaScript, read console.log in the Console, meet null from a mistyped selector, and change three elements on a page of their own. time: 50 timing: Predict and Run 10 min · Investigate 15 min · Modify 10 min · Make 15 min goals: - I can find an element on a page with JavaScript. - I can change its text and its colour. - I can read the Console to see what my code did. before: > Read the unit primer first. Students know HTML and CSS (and, from p5.js, variables and functions); this is the first time JavaScript meets a page. `document.querySelector` takes a CSS-style selector as text: `#id`, `.class`, or a tag. `textContent` is the words, `style.color` and `style.fontSize` the look. The script sits below the elements it finds: it runs when the browser reaches it. The bug task is the most common slip of the whole course: a selector that matches nothing returns `null`, and the error appears on the next line. The playground says so in its hint. Our playground runs the whole page again each time you press Run, so changes made by the script always start from the HTML. running: - "Predict: ask what the page looks like before the script runs, and after." - "Run: point out the Console under the page and where the message came from." - "Investigate: for the bug, ask 'what does querySelector give you when it finds nothing?'" - "Modify: ask students to say the selector aloud: 'hash for id, dot for class'." - "Make: ask each student which element they found first and how they knew its selector." stuck: - see: Cannot set properties of null. ask: Does the selector match the id or class exactly, with fix: Copy the id or class from the HTML, and add - see: Nothing changes, and there is no error. ask: Did you press Run, and is the change on a line after the selector? fix: Press Run again, and check the line that changes the element is inside the script. - see: The colour or size does not change. ask: Is the value in quotes and spelled as CSS spells it? fix: Write el.style.color = "red"; and el.style.fontSize = "24px"; (capital S in fontSize). - see: The page shows the script as text. ask: Is the code inside ? fix: Wrap the JavaScript in script tags. stretch: Change the page title in the browser tab with document.title, or change an element's background with style.backgroundColor. support: Give the first two lines (find, then change) and ask students to copy the pattern for each other element. leads: "Next lesson: events, so the change happens when someone clicks." exit: q: What does querySelector give you if nothing matches? a: "null, which has no textContent: that is why the next line fails." explain: > 1. `document.querySelector("#title")` finds the element with id title (`.` for a class). 2. `title.textContent = "…"` replaces its words; `title.style.color = "…"` changes its colour. 3. A script runs when the browser reaches it, so it goes below the elements it uses. solutions: step-4#t1: page.html#sol-note step-4#t2: page.html#sol-colour step-5: page.html#sol-make struggle: The selector is text and a typo gives null, with the error one line later. Teach 'null means check the selector' before anything else. ```
